They promised the party of the century. A private island in the Bahamas, supermodels, private jets and luxury villas. This is how Fyre Festival sold a dream. Billy McFarland was a young New York entrepreneur with big dreams. Then he teamed up with the rapper Ja Rule, and they built an app called Fyre. To make it famous, Billy planned a music festival on an island. They flew the biggest supermodels in the world to the Bahamas and filmed them on yachts and white sand. Then, on one single day, hundreds of influencers posted a simple orange square. Kendall Jenner was reportedly paid two hundred and fifty thousand dollars for one post. Tickets went from about five hundred dollars, up to twelve thousand dollars for a VIP package. Thousands of people bought in. But there was a problem. Billy had no festival. Follow for part two.
